title: Use animal GPS tracks to model home range to understand where they are and how they move over time
method: Project 150 191 elk GPS fixes (68 animals) to UTM 11N. Minimum bounding geometry: convex hull of all fixes (population home range, 10 607 km2) plus one hull per animal. Binned Gaussian kernel density (bandwidth 468.8 m, 200 m cells). DBSCAN (eps 500 m, min_samples 100): 91 clusters, 17.6 % noise. Overlay density, hulls and clusters on one map.

key_parameters.hull: convex hull of all fixes (+ per ind_ident)

benchmark_defects: An empty file dataset/Elk_in_MBG.geojson (0 bytes) is shipped with the inputs and cannot be read.
Data are in geographic coordinates; no CRS/units guidance is given although bandwidth and DBSCAN distance must be metric.
The published reference script passes bandwidth=468.805 to KernelDensity on the coordinates as read, without re-projection, and clusters with HDBSCAN, whereas the instruction names DBSCAN.
checks: required: a captured polygon layer matches the convex hull of all fixes or the union of per-animal hulls (area IoU >= 0.90)

required: a captured 2-D density array (assumed to span the fix extent, padded or not, either row order) correlates with the gold KDE (Pearson on sqrt density >= 0.6, 40 x 40 grid), or a per-fix density vector has Spearman >= 0.7; the array must be kernel-smoothed (corr with its own 3x3 mean >= 0.9, rejects raw histograms); runs with no 2-D array: a kdeplot / kernel-density + contour call in the code is accepted
required: a label vector of the fixes with noise (-1), >= 2 clusters and >= 90 % nearest-neighbour label agreement

required (as in task 43): a DBSCAN / HDBSCAN / OPTICS call in the code (import alone does not count; DBSCAN named with eps/min_samples accepted when the call sits in a block missing from the checked code)
required: Elk_Analysis.png (the figure written last to that name) overlays a hull outline, a density layer and a cluster layer
optional: a projected CRS is used in the code
optional, kind=figure: a density image drawn in the saved map, placed as drawn (extent + origin), agrees with the gold KDE at least as well as its north-south mirror
